liquidGL

A framework-free JavaScript library by NaughtyDuk that renders refracting glass panes over live web content with WebGPU or WebGL.

Context

The README: liquidGL “turns any fixed or sticky-positioned element into a perfectly refracted, glossy ‘glass pane’ rendered in WebGPU (with automatic fallback to WebGL)”, and “recreates Apple’s ‘Liquid Glass’ aesthetic in the browser”. It falls back to CSS backdrop-filter and offers tint, chromatic aberration, and stacked lenses. GitHub.

The LICENSE file is MIT, “Copyright (c) NaughtyDuk”. Wikipedia calls it the most actively maintained of the widely used web implementations as of September 2026. Wikipedia: Liquid Glass.

Observed

  • A photo of a red running track with the legs of runners and their shadows.
  • Six rounded glass tiles form a fitness dashboard: distance, heart rate (a large “137 BPM”), speed, power, resistance, and an interval delta. Labels are small uppercase white sans-serif with green accents.
  • Each tile has a bevelled rim where the track texture and the white lane line bend and magnify. The line through the heart-rate tile kinks at the tile edge.
  • Rims catch thin highlights, and the tiles keep the red-brown color of the track. A large white “liquidGL” wordmark sits at the lower right.

Why it belongs

The library shows that the refraction can be reproduced on the web, but only with a shader and an offscreen copy of the page, not with CSS alone.

Borrow

Concentrate the distortion in a narrow bevel and keep the center of the pane flat, so text inside stays readable.
